Marathon Petroleum stock rose 0.31% today in a market shaped by tightening global refinery capacity and elevated oil prices. U.S. crude is trading at $91.48 per barrel—well above historical norms—while diesel reached record highs this week as the Ukraine and Iran conflicts have knocked refineries offline, particularly in Russia. Refineries in the U.S. are running at 98% capacity, near their practical limit, which means tight supplies and strong prices for refined products like gasoline and diesel that Marathon produces and sells.

The broader backdrop has tightened significantly over the past two weeks: geopolitical escalation in the Middle East (with Iran sanctions intensifying and the U.S. pursuing a deal in Venezuela for oil supplies) has removed refining capacity from the global market, driving the 7.81% run-up in the stock since August 28th. For a refiner, this environment—constrained supply, high crude prices, and refineries running flat out—typically improves profit margins on the fuel they crack from crude oil.
